title: Distribution Reward overpayments must be repaid by the Prime Agent, which can only recoup them from future rewards
content:
A.2.2.9.1.2.1.3.4 handles calculation errors asymmetrically. "Underpayments are resolved retroactively" — the recipient is made whole. "In cases of overpayment, the Prime Agent associated with the affected Reward Code must reimburse Sky the overpayment amount and can use future Distribution Reward payments to reimburse itself."

The Prime Agent is therefore the residual risk bearer for a measurement process it does not run. Distribution Rewards are calculated by Operational GovOps (A.2.2.9.1.2.1.3.3.1), under Tracking Methodologies that A.2.2.9.1.2.1.1.2.4 permits Agents *and* Operational GovOps to develop. An error introduced anywhere in that chain lands on the Agent's balance sheet.

The self-reimbursement clause reveals the intended cash-flow shape: the Agent pays Sky now and recovers from its own future reward stream, so an overpayment is effectively a forward assignment of revenue. That works while the Agent's Reward Codes keep producing, and does not if the underlying balances have left.

The sharpest exposure comes from combining this with A.2.2.4.2, which pays all Integrator rewards to the Prime Agent with any share to the Integrator "subject to bilateral negotiation" and no obligation to share. A Prime Agent that has already passed a negotiated portion to an Integrator owes Sky the full overpayment while having no Atlas-level claim to recover the passed-through part. Placing the duty on the Prime is administratively clean — one accountable counterparty per Reward Code — but the Agent absorbs both the calculation risk and the counterparty risk of its own partners.
description: Underpayments are fixed retroactively, but tracking errors in the Agent's favour become the Agent's debt to Sky — even though the Integrator may have already received a share.
